## What we know

- **Name:** 正蓝旗护军营房 Zhenglan qi hujun yingfang (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03 · confidence A)
- **In English:** Plain Blue Banner guard camp (蓝旗营) (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03)
- **What it was:** a camp of the banner guard outside the garden walls (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03 · confidence A)
- **In 1860:** in use; seen 6 Oct 1860, held by the soldiers' families, the men away with Senggerinqin (S241 p.286, if this is the camp Swinhoe saw) (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03)
- **Size:** 1250 jian (1724) + 300 jian (1747) (S1237) (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03)
- **Where:** today's place names 正蓝旗 (osm node 13239886792) and 蓝旗营 (osm node 10548036958); S1008 蓝旗营: S of 清华's south wall by 清华南门; C (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03 · confidence A)
- **Note:** 八旗通志 '坐落保福寺'; 日下 j99:24a '南海淀之東有正藍旗護軍營房' and 保福寺 '南海淀之東二里許'. Swinhoe S241 p.286 (A, 1860): 'a large cluster of low houses, enclosed by an eight-feet wall, and entered by a large wooden gate', a few houses outside the wall right of the gate: the British cavalry's 'barracks of the Blue Bannermen' on the way from the 德胜门 north road NW to the palace; identification with this camp C (it is the only blue camp on that line; 镶蓝旗 lay far SW). S02 p.56-57 plates: its south gate and the 关帝庙 court inside its north gate. (S1237, S05, S1008, S02, S241, S03)
